description: The kit's health report from a native app wrapper: as viewer2, a report with WebVersion null and a valid Client (what a native app wrapper such as Jellyfin Media Player sends, whose appVersion() is its own version) is accepted; a report with a bad Client is dropped first, and doesn't use up viewer2's one report per ten minutes. Run after health-missing-anchor.json; health-diagnostics.json checks what the server kept.

steps.name: a bad Client (dropped), then WebVersion null with a valid Client (accepted): both answered 204
steps.script: const api = window.__jfkit.jfbm.instance.api; const native = { WebVersion: null, Client: 'Jellyfin Media Player', ClientVersion: '1.12.0', Layout: 'Desktop', Experimental: false, PluginVersion: '1.0.0.0', Missing: [{ Anchor: 'detailButtons', View: 'details', Count: 1 }] }; const bad = Object.assign({}, native, { Client: 'Jellyfin Media Player; DROP' }); return [await api('POST', 'Bookmarks/Diagnostics/ClientHealth', { body: bad }), await api('POST', 'Bookmarks/Diagnostics/ClientHealth', { body: native })];

steps.name: no uncaught exceptions (the stale CustomRatings tag excepted)
